item.research_question: How does the number of metallic elements in multi-component high-entropy alloys affect their resistance to interdiffusion between Cu and Si, and what are the structural and thermodynamic mechanisms responsible for this suppression?
item.material_system: Six alloy systems: unitary Ti (1A), binary TiTa (2A), ternary TiTaCr (3A), quaternary TiTaCrZr (4A), quinary TiTaCrZrAl (5A), and senary TiTaCrZrAlRu (6A); used as ~7 nm diffusion barrier layers (DBnA) in Si/DBnA/Cu stacks.
item.processing_route: Magnetron sputtering at room temperature; RF power 150 W, substrate bias -100 V, Ar atmosphere (30 sccm, 6 × 10⁻³ torr); Cu top layer (50 nm) deposited at 50 W; thermal annealing in N₂/H₂ (5% H₂) at 300–900°C for 30 min (5°C/min ramp).
item.test_conditions: Thermal annealing from 300°C to 900°C; failure defined by Cu penetration into Si forming Cu silicides; characterized via SEM, XRD, electrical resistivity, TEM, and EDS line scanning.
key_findings: Failure temperature of Si/DBnA/Cu stacks increased from 550°C (unitary Ti) to 900°C (senary TiTaCrZrAlRu) with more elements.
Activation energy of Cu diffusion increased from 110 kJ/mol (unitary) to 163 kJ/mol (senary), a difference of 53 kJ/mol.
Lattice distortion strain energy increased to 16.8 kJ/mol for quaternary alloys and remained high (11.9–14.6 kJ/mol) for quinary/senary alloys.
Average cohesive energy increased by up to 38.1 kJ/mol in the senary alloy compared to the unitary alloy (14.2 kJ/mol).
Packing density increased from 0.680 (bcc-based binary) to 0.711 (senary), reducing free volume and vacancy concentration.
Theoretical total increase in activation energy (55 kJ/mol) closely matched the experimental increase (53 kJ/mol).
Amorphous senary alloy remained stable up to 800°C, whereas unitary Ti crystallized at 500°C.
item.mechanism: Suppressed interdiffusion is caused by three dominant factors: (1) structural lattice distortion strain energy elongates diffusion paths and increases vacancy formation difficulty; (2) increased cohesive energy raises the bond-breaking energy required for atom movement; and (3) higher packing density reduces free volume, diminishing vacancy concentration. Together, these thermodynamic and structural factors increase the activation energy for substitutional Cu diffusion via vacancies.
item.limitations: Small differences between experimental and theoretical activation energies may be attributable to a 'volume-to-area' effect, as diffusion models are typically 2D while calculations are 3D; also, exact composition of thin barriers may slightly vary from thick films due to thickness dependence.
item.future_work: Further investigation is needed to clarify the possibility of short-range ordering existing within the amorphous matrix of the alloy barriers.
quotes: with more elements incorporated, the failure temperature of the barriers increased from 550 to 900°C.
the activation energy of Cu diffusion through the alloy barriers was determined to increase from 110 to 163 kJ/mole.

structurally, severe lattice distortion strains and a high packing density caused by different atom sizes, and, thermodynamically, a strengthened cohesion provide a total increase of 55 kJ/mole in the activation energy of substitutional Cu diffusion
